entries.title: How This Newsroom Holds Evidence Instead of Headlines
entries.subtitle: A worked example of the reasoning engine, using this repository's own build as the case study
entries.author: Omoluabi News — Editorial
entries.excerpt: This is a demonstration story, not a field report. It walks the twelve reasoning layers through the record of how this site itself was built.
entries.content:
This story is an example, not a report on a real-world event. It exists so a reader can see the reasoning engine work on something fully verifiable: the history of this repository.

On 2 July 2026, a repository restoration pass audited this repository and found it effectively empty — the only tracked file was .gitattributes. That audit is still in the repository. On 7 July 2026, this pass added the visual system, the reasoning and timeline engines, the data schema, this story, and the GitHub Actions deployment workflow described below.

Every claim above can be checked against the repository's own commit history and audit file — nothing here is asserted without a source a reader can open themselves.

entries.title: Who Gets to Name a Species? The Case of Leopardus tilcayo
entries.subtitle: An Omoluabi investigation into what changes when locally held knowledge becomes formal scientific taxonomy.
entries.author: Omoluabi News — Research POC
entries.excerpt: Local communities already knew the tilcayo. Genomics made the lineage formally visible to science. This POC traces the authority shift from local knowledge to taxonomy, media and conservation.
entries.content: Local communities in Bolivia's Yungas already used the name tilcayo. In 2026, genomic evidence supported its formal description as Leopardus tilcayo. Omoluabi separates being known, being observed and being institutionally classified, then follows what that shift changes for conservation and the historical record.
erasedContexts: The animal was locally known and named before formal scientific description
entries.primaryTimeline: Local knowledge predates the 2016 sanctuary observation and the 2026 taxonomic publication

entries.title: The Energy War: Power, Fuel and the Story of the Strike
entries.subtitle: A developing Omoluabi investigation into energy as civilian survival system, war infrastructure and a contested public story.
entries.author: Omoluabi News — Developing Investigation
entries.excerpt: An opening distortion map traces how energy events become public claims, and how UN monitoring, energy data, nuclear-safety records and local testimony can keep the evidence in view.
entries.content: Energy in Russia’s war on Ukraine is at once a survival system, a military and economic resource, and a subject of competing claims. This developing investigation follows those threads while keeping each claim tied to its evidence and limits.
expectedVoices: People with disabilities and others who rely on power-dependent services
Civilians affected by energy disruptions in Russia, where verifiable access is possible
erasedContexts: The daily consequences of outages for people who depend on electricity, heating, water, mobility aids, or medical services
The distinction between infrastructure damage and independently measured military effects
The limits on independent assessment of Ukrainian strikes inside Russia
entries.primaryTimeline: A developing chronology of attacks, outages, repairs, fuel and policy changes; incident dates and effects will be entered only when supported by evidence.
